title: DNA replication; Food tests and chromatography
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: BM09a#t4 term and clue written for the game; GE01b#t4 term and clue written for the game; BM09a#t3 term and clue written for the game; BM09a#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: BM09a#N.4b, GE01b#N.7, BM09a#N.14, GE01b#N.9, GE01b#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Reducing sugars
items.clue: Group made up of all monosaccharides plus maltose and lactose

items.label: Hybrid DNA
items.clue: Intermediate band: one ¹⁵N strand paired with one ¹⁴N strand.

items.label: Biuret test
items.clue: A change from blue to lilac shows that peptide bonds are present

items.label: Iodine test
items.clue: A change from orange-brown to blue-black shows that starch is present

questions.stem: Four solutions, W, X, Y and Z, were each heated with the same volume of Benedict's reagent for the same time. Final colours: W orange, X blue, Y brick red, Z green. Which list puts them in order of reducing sugar concentration, lowest first?

options.text: Y, W, Z, X
X, Z, W, Y
X, W, Z, Y
Z, X, W, Y

questions.explanation: Blue (none) → green → orange → brick red (most). The more reducing sugar, the more Cu²⁺ is reduced to red copper(I) oxide.

questions.stem: A double-stranded DNA molecule in which both strands contain only heavy nitrogen (¹⁵N) is replicated three times in a medium that supplies only light nitrogen (¹⁴N), producing 8 DNA molecules. How many of the 8 DNA molecules contain any ¹⁵N?

options.text: 1 of 8
8 of 8
2 of 8
4 of 8

questions.explanation: In round 1 the two ¹⁵N strands separate and each pairs with a new ¹⁴N strand. They stay intact in every later round, so after round 3, 2 molecules contain ¹⁵N and 6 contain only ¹⁴N.

questions.stem: A sample of milk is tested. Heated with Benedict's reagent: an orange-red precipitate. With biuret reagent: lilac. With iodine in potassium iodide: stays orange-brown. Which conclusion is supported?

options.text: It contains glucose and no other sugar.
It contains starch, protein and a reducing sugar.
It contains a reducing sugar and protein, but no detectable lipid.
It contains a reducing sugar and protein, but no detectable starch.

questions.explanation: Precipitate: reducing sugar. Lilac: peptide bonds, so protein. No blue-black: no starch detected.

questions.stem: In the Meselson–Stahl experiment, which result after one generation in ¹⁴N would have supported the conservative model?

options.text: One band, of intermediate density.
Two bands of equal amount, one heavy and one light.
One band, heavy.
Two bands of equal amount, one intermediate and one light.

questions.explanation: Conservative keeps the parent molecule whole (heavy) and makes a completely new one (light): two bands, equal amounts.

questions.stem: The experiment is run in reverse. Bacteria are grown for many generations on light nitrogen (¹⁴N), then moved to a medium containing only heavy nitrogen (¹⁵N). Replication is semi-conservative. What will the DNA show after two generations on ¹⁵N?

options.text: Two bands of equal amount: intermediate and light.
Two bands of equal amount: intermediate and heavy.
One band, between intermediate and heavy.
Two bands: one quarter light, three quarters heavy.

questions.explanation: Generation 1: every molecule is one light + one heavy strand (intermediate). Generation 2: 4 molecules, 2 hybrids holding the old light strands and 2 all-heavy.
